plan: In a single-round sealed bid auction with rational opponents, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically near my private value. Since my value is $31, I want to win without overpaying. I'll bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Rational opponents will also bid strategically. I'll choose a bid that balances winning probability with profit margin - around $28-$30 seems optimal to create a buffer against overpaying while still having a strong chance of winning.

With a private value of $31, I want to maximize potential profit. Since this is a single round with no prior history, I'll use a strategic approach: bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. Rational opponents will likely bid near their own values. I'll aim to bid around $25-$28 to potentially win while minimizing overpayment. This leaves room for profit if I win and minimizes loss if I don't.

With a private value of $46, I want to win the auction but minimize my payment. Other rational bidders will likely bid strategically based on their own values. I'll aim to bid slightly above the expected second-highest bid. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, the expected competing bid might be around $25-$35. I'll bid $35 to increase my chances of winning while preserving potential profit.
